scenarios.claim: Real producer process SIGKILLed after the authoritative local commit (Trip DRIVER_ACCEPTED + Saga AUTHORIZE_PENDING + pending AuthorizePaymentV1) and before publication, at the Saga.AfterPersistBeforeDispatch faultpoint; a new process on the same database/broker reclaims the orphaned claim and publishes the SAME messageId with intact sagaId/operationKey lineage; no second logical transition.

Process killed after durable authorize dispatch; Payment success backlogs on the quorum queue while the service is down (consumers 0, ready 1); the restarted process continues the SAME saga (identity, operationKey, StepVersion+1 exactly) through READY_TO_START → IN_PROGRESS → COMPLETED → CAPTURED/COMPLETED; stale DECLINED and duplicate capture outcomes cannot regress terminal state.

Late DriverReservedV1 on a CANCELLED trip through the real broker: no reactivation, exact ReleaseDriverReservationV1 cleanup for the late reservation identity; a logically duplicate delivery (fresh messageId, same fact) is a durable BusinessReplay with no second mutation or intent.

Authorization success after cancellation through the real process: Trip stays CANCELLED, exact VoidPaymentAuthorizationV1 with the frozen void key ({tripId}:void:v1) and exact sagaId lineage; void then release legs resolve in order to terminal COMPENSATED only when both resolved.

Process crashed with the release obligation outstanding (DECLINED path); the Driver release confirmation backlogs while the service is down; after restart the exact reservation identity resolves compensation to COMPENSATED; no void obligation ever existed on the DECLINED path.

Faultpoint disabled by default; double-gated activation (config + non-Production, fail-fast in Production); loud misconfiguration; gate holds only activated saga dispatches, writes the observable reached marker, releases on signal, never blocks past its deadline; relay seam wired exactly when enabled.

limitations: Payment outcomes are produced by the test harness acting as the Payment authority publisher (exact lineage carried); the real Payment service leg is C-W10-pending and is never faked as delivered.
Driver authority facts (reserved/released/started/completed) are produced by the harness; Driver-side authoritative state effects belong to B and are not claimed here.

The producer-commit artifacts for scenarios that require DRIVER_ACCEPTED (no transport exists yet for driver acceptance) are seeded through the real handler chain in one transaction — the identical rows the service itself commits — and every scenario asserts the committed pre-crash state through the real process's relay/consumer before the crash.

REL-04's dispatch window is held by the faultpoint; a claim-lease window of 2s is configured for the restarted process so reclaim is fast (Outbox:ClaimLeaseSeconds), which is configuration, not a timing assumption.
